authors.bio: Madeleine Noland is president of the Advanced Television Systems Committee, Washington, D.C. (mnoland@atsc.org). Widely respected for her consensus-building leadership style, she chaired the ATSC Technology Group that oversees the ATSC 3.0 broadcast standard before being named ATSC president in May 2019. Previously, as a representative of LG Electronics, she has chaired various ATSC 3.0-related specialist groups, ad hoc groups, and implementation teams since 2012. A 15-year industry veteran, she held key technology management and standards roles at BackChannelMedia Inc., TelVue Corp., and LG. She received the TVNewsCheck ’s “2019 Futurist” Women in Technology Award and was named one of 2018’s “Powerful Women in Consumer Technology” by Dealerscope. In 2016, she received the ATSC’s highest technical honor, the Bernard J. Lechner Outstanding Contributor Award. She graduated cum laude from the University of Massachusetts, Boston, MA.
authors.name: Madeleine Noland

authors.bio: Jerry Whitaker is the vice president for Standards Development, Advanced Television Systems Committee (jwhitaker@atsc.org). He supports the work of the various ATSC technology and specialist groups and assists in the development of ATSC standards and related documents. He currently serves as a secretary of the Technology Group on Next Generation Broadcast Television and is closely involved in work related to educational programs. He is a Fellow of the Society of Broadcast Engineers (SBE) and a Life Fellow of SMPTE. He has served as a board member and vice president of the SBE.
authors.name: Jerry Whitaker
